description_en:
This mixed reality artwork introduces a hidden layer of surreal, AI-generated objects into the viewer's physical environment. Built as a standalone Android application specifically for the Meta Quest 3, the piece requires only the headset (HMD) and it's video passthrough features to experience, offering a completely untethered encounter. Leveraging the device's high-fidelity passthrough, the artwork allows users to physically manifest a biome of steampunk insects and non-existent flora from thin air. The experience is deeply rooted in the "dreamcore" aesthetic, designed to evoke anemoia—a profound nostalgia for times and places that never actually existed.

In this piece, generative AI serves as both a technical foundation and a conceptual partner, used to express ambiguous human emotions that defy verbal articulation. Initial visions of these impossible organisms are generated using Nano Banana Pro by the artist using text prompts to capture the specific dreamcore visual style. These 2D concepts are then reconstructed into 3D gaussian splatting assets using SAM3D object models by the artist. Conceptually, the AI acts as a conduit to the subconscious, externalizing complex feelings into entities that feel oddly familiar yet belong to an inaccessible world.

The interaction design introduces the principle of "Dream Logic Affordance," mapping physical human action to magical reaction. Using a custom VFX toolkit, the user's bare-hand tracking data directly drives specific shader uniforms. For instance, a "Hand Openness" parameter controls a radial expansion effect: closing a fist causes a steampunk creature to entropy into digital particles, while opening the hand triggers a rolling reveal to summon it back. By ensuring these entities obey magical laws rather than physical ones, this self-contained installation immerses users in a tactile, emotionally resonant dreamscape where the boundaries between reality, AI generation, and pure imagination dissolve.

A demo video is publically avaliable on Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vL4X_rGzktQ
(The background music in thde video is created by the artist using Eleven Labs)
description_cn:
这件混合现实作品在观众所处的物理环境中引入了一层隐秘的、由 AI 生成的超现实物体。作品为 Meta Quest 3 专门开发成独立的 Android 应用，体验时只需头显及其视频透视功能，无需外接设备。借助设备高精度的 passthrough，观众可以仿佛从空气中召唤出由蒸汽朋克昆虫与不存在的植物组成的生态群落。作品深植于“dreamcore”美学，旨在唤起 anemoia：一种对从未真实存在过的时代与地点产生的深切怀旧。

在这件作品中，生成式 AI 既是技术基础，也是概念上的协作者，用以表达难以用语言准确描述的暧昧情感。艺术家首先通过文本提示，使用 Nano Banana Pro 生成这些不可能生物的初始视觉图像，以捕捉特定的 dreamcore 视觉风格；随后再借助 SAM3D object models，将二维概念图重建为 3D Gaussian Splatting 资产。从概念层面看，AI 像是通往潜意识的媒介，将复杂情绪外化为既陌生又似曾相识、仿佛来自不可抵达世界的实体。

作品的交互设计引入了“梦逻辑可供性”（Dream Logic Affordance）的原则，将人的身体动作映射为魔法般的回应。通过定制 VFX 工具包，用户裸手追踪数据会直接驱动特定 shader 参数。例如，“手掌张开程度”控制径向扩张效果：握拳时，蒸汽朋克生物会熵化为数字粒子；再次张开手掌时，它又以翻卷显现的方式被召回。通过让这些实体服从魔法法则而非物理法则，这件自成一体的装置将观众带入一个触觉化、富有情感共鸣的梦境空间，在其中现实、AI 生成与纯粹想象之间的边界逐渐消融。

作品演示视频已公开于 YouTube：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vL4X_rGzktQ
（视频背景音乐由艺术家使用 Eleven Labs 创作）
artist_bio_en:
cocolinux is a technical artist and mixed reality researcher based in Hamburg, Germany, working at the intersection of immersive media and cutting-edge rendering technologies. Her artistic practice focuses on bringing the dreamcore aesthetic to spatial computing, utilizing the latest advancements in generative world models and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Through her visual effects, she seeks to trigger anemoia, a profound sense of nostalgia for times and spaces that never actually existed. Her dreamcore piece, Snow After Us, was awarded third place at the inaugural World Labs Winter Competition in 2026.

Beyond her personal artwork, cocolinux bridges the gap between research and practical development. She created the first commercially adopted 3DGS shader and VFX toolkit for Unity. Featuring advanced volumetric relighting, this toolkit currently supports over 150 studios and independent developers worldwide. In academia, her research on radiance field rendering, spatial interactions, and intelligent virtual agents is frequently published at top international venues like TVCG, ISMAR, IEEE VR, and IROS. She also actively contributes to the XR research community, serving on the international program committees for premier conferences, including IEEE VR 2026 and ISMAR 2026.

artist_bio_cn:
cocolinux 是一位常驻德国汉堡的技术美术与混合现实研究员，主要在沉浸式媒体与前沿渲染技术的交汇处进行探索。她的艺术实践侧重于将梦核美学引入空间计算领域，并结合生成式世界模型与3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）的最新技术进展。通过视觉特效的创作，她希望能触发一种名为“anemoia”的情感共鸣，即对从未真实存在过的时空所产生的怀旧感。2026年，其梦核主题作品《Snow After Us》在首届 World Labs 冬季竞赛中获得了季军。

在个人创作之外，cocolinux 也致力于将技术研究转化为实际应用。她开发了首个投入商业使用的、适用于Unity的3DGS着色器与视觉特效工具包。该工具包具备高级体积重光照功能，目前有幸为全球150多家工作室和独立开发者提供技术支持。在学术领域，她关于辐射场渲染与交互以及虚拟智能体的研究工作，曾多次发表于 TVCG、ISMAR、IEEE VR 和 IROS 等国际重要学术会议与期刊。此外，她也积极参与学术界的服务工作，在 IEEE VR 2026 和 ISMAR 2026 等相关领域的重要学术会议中担任国际学术委员会成员。

description_en:
Abject Space by Adam Nash is a large-scale augmented reality artwork where visitors "dance the work into existence." Moving through an architectural volume holding phones or tablets, visitors trigger the spawning of semi-transparent 3D shapes (each with precisely determined colour, scale, spatial position, and spatialised audio unique to that visitor) accumulating into abstract audiovisual "paintings" that emerge from traces of human movement through space.

The artwork is authored by the artist through intricate, interdependent rule systems governing every visual and sonic parameter. Visitors are performers, discovering the work by moving through it. Shapes obey rules for formation geometry, colour palettes, pitch, volume envelopes, temporal persistence, and spatial density, rules that propagate and interact to produce emergent complexity from simple foundations. Space itself pushes back: an occupancy system creates organic density limits, so the artwork develops material resistance as it fills.

AI is integrated at every level of the work's creation. The codebase is written collaboratively with Claude Code; rather than merely a tool that produces the art, code here is the very stuff of the art itself. An evolutionary algorithm coupled with machine-learning preference modelling allows the artist to train the system's aesthetic sensibility through selection alone, without explicit articulation. The project also tracks its own AI energy footprint, and this data feeds directly back into the composition: energy consumed during creation influences palette, formation density, pitch, and volume envelope. The material cost of AI becomes compositional material.

This feedback loop is central to the work's title. The infrastructure that makes contemporary AI possible (servers, power, water, labour) is normally hidden from view. In Abject Space, what is hidden returns through the artwork's own visual and sonic language: what AI conceals becomes what visitors see and hear as they create it.
description_cn:
Adam Nash 的《Abject Space》是一件大型增强现实作品，观众通过“舞动”让作品生成。观众手持手机或平板穿行于建筑体量之中，会触发半透明三维形体的生成；每个形体都拥有为该观众精确设定的颜色、尺度、空间位置与空间化声音，并逐渐累积成由人体在空间中的移动痕迹生成的抽象视听“绘画”。

作品由艺术家通过复杂且相互依赖的规则系统编写而成，规则支配着每一个视觉与声音参数。观众既是表演者，也是在移动中发现作品的人。形体遵循关于生成几何、色彩调色板、音高、音量包络、时间持续性与空间密度的规则；这些规则彼此传播、交互，使作品从简单基础中生成涌现的复杂性。空间本身也会“反作用”于作品：占用系统会形成有机的密度上限，使作品在不断填充时发展出一种材料般的阻力。

AI 被整合进作品创作的每一个层面。代码库由艺术家与 Claude Code 协作编写；在这里，代码不只是生产艺术的工具，而是艺术本身的材料。一个结合机器学习偏好建模的进化算法，使艺术家能够仅通过选择来训练系统的审美感受，而无需明确阐述规则。项目还追踪自身的 AI 能源足迹，并将这些数据直接反馈进构成之中：创作过程中消耗的能量会影响色彩、形体密度、音高与音量包络。AI 的物质成本由此成为构图材料。

这一反馈回路正是作品标题的核心。当代 AI 得以运作的基础设施，如服务器、电力、水与劳动，通常被隐藏在视线之外。在《Abject Space》中，被隐藏之物通过作品自身的视觉与声音语言返回现场：AI 所遮蔽的，成为观众在共同生成作品时所看见和听见的。
artist_bio_en:
Adam Nash makes mixed-reality playable art. He is internationally recognized as one of the most original artists working in digital virtual environments, sound art, performance and extended-reality technology. He uses generative programming, motion capture, composition and live performance.

He has exhibited and performed in galleries, festivals and online all over the world, including SIGGRAPH, ISEA, 01SJ, Venice Biennale, National Gallery of Victoria and National Portrait Gallery of Australia.  An early innovator in mixed-reality and online performance and exhibition, he won the inaugural Australia Council Multi-User Virtual Environment Artist in Residence grant. He won the SIGGRAPH Web3D Art jury prize three years running. He was shortlisted for the National Art Award in New Media. He was artist in residence at Ars Electronica FutureLab, Neutral Ground and the Australian Antarctic Division.

He was awarded an Australia Council Connections Residency, with John McCormick. For this, they founded Wild System, developing AI-driven mixed-reality performance collaborations between virtual environments, natural systems and robots.

He was composer and sound artist with Machine Movement Lab, Company In Space and Gibson/Martelli, exploring integrations of motion capture with realtime 3D audiovisual spaces. He was composer for NYID, performer/composer for The Men Who Knew Too Much and performer for TN! Theatre Company. He has performed with many bands.

He has a PhD from the Centre for Animation and Interactive Media at RMIT University, Melbourne, Australia, researching multi-user virtual environments. He was Associate Professor of Virtual Interior in the School of Architecture and Urban Design at RMIT University. Previously he was Associate Dean of Digital Design in the School of Design at RMIT University. At the end of 2021, he resigned from academia to concentrate on art making. He was awarded the rank of Honorary University Fellow. He is also a Master Tree Grower and active member of the Heytesbury District Landcare Network.
artist_bio_cn:
Adam Nash 创作可游玩的混合现实艺术。他被国际公认为在数字虚拟环境、声音艺术、表演和扩展现实技术领域最具原创性的艺术家之一，其作品运用生成式编程、动作捕捉、作曲和现场表演。

他的作品曾在全球各地的画廊、艺术节及线上平台展出和演出，包括 SIGGRAPH、ISEA、01SJ、威尼斯双年展、维多利亚国家美术馆和澳大利亚国家肖像美术馆。作为混合现实与线上表演、展览的早期创新者，他曾获得首届 Australia Council Multi-User Virtual Environment Artist in Residence 资助，并连续三年获得 SIGGRAPH Web3D Art 评审奖。他曾入围 National Art Award in New Media，并担任 Ars Electronica FutureLab、Neutral Ground 与 Australian Antarctic Division 的驻留艺术家。

他曾与 John McCormick 一同获得 Australia Council Connections Residency，并由此共同创立 Wild System，发展由 AI 驱动的混合现实表演协作，将虚拟环境、自然系统与机器人连接起来。

他也曾作为作曲家和声音艺术家与 Machine Movement Lab、Company In Space、Gibson/Martelli 合作，探索动作捕捉与实时三维视听空间的整合。他曾为 NYID 作曲，担任 The Men Who Knew Too Much 的表演者/作曲者，并参与 TN! Theatre Company 的演出，也曾与多个乐队合作演出。

Adam Nash 获有澳大利亚墨尔本 RMIT University 动画与互动媒体中心博士学位，研究方向为多用户虚拟环境。他曾任 RMIT University 建筑与城市设计学院 Virtual Interior 副教授，也曾任设计学院数字设计副院长。2021 年底，他离开学术界，专注于艺术创作，并获授 Honorary University Fellow 称号。他同时也是 Master Tree Grower，并积极参与 Heytesbury District Landcare Network。

description_en:
Arc de Resonance is a new mixed reality artwork by Uncalculated Studio that merges speculative architecture, immersive sound, and participatory digital experience into a surreal public encounter. Developed across Maya, Unreal Engine, and Unity, the work invites audiences to step beneath a monumental virtual arc whose apex is crowned by a winged, single-eyed angelic figure suspended between the sacred, synthetic, and cinematic.

Conceived as a contemporary “selfie experience,” Arc de Resonance explores how identity, performance, and memory are increasingly shaped through screen culture and networked image-making. Visitors are encouraged to physically position themselves beneath the arc, becoming momentary participants within the artwork’s symbolic geometry. The installation transforms the audience from passive observers into active performers, generating personal images and shared social encounters that extend the work beyond the exhibition space itself.

The project combines sculptural digital aesthetics with atmospheric sound design through an original soundtrack by Uncalculated Studio titled Sunshine Cloud, composed specifically for the exhibition. Using AI to provide the roadmap for animating in Unity, this work explores synthetic intelligence as a co-creative partner. The music blends shimmering melodic textures, layered frequencies, and emotionally resonant ambient rhythms that respond to the dreamlike visual environment. Together, the sound and imagery create a contemplative space that oscillates between digital ritual, speculative mythology, and immersive entertainment.

Visually, the winged figure references both ancient cosmological iconography and contemporary virtual avatars, collapsing distinctions between spiritual symbolism and computational imagery. The singular eye positioned at the zenith of the structure evokes themes of perception, surveillance, transcendence, and machine vision, while the arc itself functions as a portal-like threshold between physical and virtual space.

Technically, Arc de Resonance reflects Uncalculated Studio’s ongoing interest in hybrid production pipelines and emergent digital aesthetics. By moving assets fluidly between Maya, Unreal Engine, and Unity, the work embraces interoperability as both a technical strategy and conceptual framework. The result is a highly accessible mixed reality artwork that combines public engagement, immersive media, and speculative world-building into a visually striking and socially shareable experience.
description_cn:
《Arc de Resonance》是 Uncalculated Studio 的一件全新混合现实作品，将推想建筑、沉浸式声音与参与式数字体验融合为一场超现实的公共遭遇。作品通过 Maya、Unreal Engine 与 Unity 开发，邀请观众站到一座纪念碑式虚拟拱门之下；拱门顶端悬置着一位带翼、独眼的天使形象，游移于神圣、合成与电影感之间。

作为一种当代“自拍体验”，《Arc de Resonance》探讨身份、表演与记忆如何日益被屏幕文化和网络化图像生产塑造。观众被鼓励将自己的身体置于拱门之下，短暂成为作品象征性几何结构中的参与者。装置将观众从被动观看者转化为主动表演者，生成个人图像与共享的社交遭遇，并将作品延展到展场之外。

项目将雕塑性的数字美学与氛围化声音设计结合在一起，声音部分来自 Uncalculated Studio 为本次展览特别创作的原创配乐《Sunshine Cloud》。作品使用 AI 为 Unity 动画制作提供路线图，探索合成智能作为共同创作者的可能。音乐融合闪烁的旋律质感、层叠的频率与富有情感共鸣的环境节奏，与梦境般的视觉环境相互呼应。声音与图像共同营造出一个沉思性的空间，在数字仪式、推想神话与沉浸式娱乐之间振荡。

在视觉上，带翼形象同时指涉古代宇宙论图像与当代虚拟化身，消解了精神象征与计算图像之间的界线。位于结构顶点的单眼唤起关于感知、监视、超越与机器视觉的主题，而拱门本身则如同连接物理与虚拟空间的门槛。

从技术层面看，《Arc de Resonance》延续了 Uncalculated Studio 对混合生产流程和涌现数字美学的兴趣。通过在 Maya、Unreal Engine 与 Unity 之间流动地转换资产，作品将互操作性既作为技术策略，也作为概念框架。最终呈现的是一件高度可进入的混合现实作品，将公共参与、沉浸式媒体与推想式世界建构结合成一种视觉鲜明且适于社交传播的体验。
artist_bio_en: UnCalculated Studio is the creative partnership of Rewa Wright and Simon Howden, two artists who bring science, sound, and storytelling together in bold, accessible ways. Working between Australia and Aotearoa/New Zealand, they create large-scale digital artworks that transform plant signals, environmental data, and cosmic phenomena into immersive experiences that animate public space and spark curiosity. With exhibitions at Ars Electronica, SIGGRAPH Los Angeles, ISEA2024, VIVID Sydney, SIGGRAPH Asia Brisbane & Daegu, the Prague Quadrennial, Messe Taoyuan, and Collingwood Yards and Federation Square 4K Digital Screen Melbourne, UnCalculated Studio is recognised for creating innovative, welcoming digital artworks that connect communities to both the cosmos and the living ecologies around them. Rewa has been working with plants and algorithms in mixed reality since 2012 and has over 25 years’ experience across moving image, interaction design and digital environments. A First Nations Māori artist (Ngai Tawake, Te Kaimaroke, Te Uri o Hau), her work weaves Indigenous knowledge with interactive media, informed by international presentations across Europe, Asia, and the Pacific. Simon is an audio-visual artist and music producer who creates bespoke soundscapes using plant bio-signals and experimental materials. He holds an MFA from Elam School of Art (University of Auckland) and, as a musician, has reached global audiences with over 45 million YouTube views and Billboard-chart collaborations with artists including Busta Rhymes, Popcaan, and Wyclef Jean.
artist_bio_cn:
UnCalculated Studio 是 Rewa Wright 与 Simon Howden 的创作组合，两位艺术家以大胆而易于亲近的方式将科学、声音与叙事结合起来。他们往来于澳大利亚与 Aotearoa/新西兰之间，创作大型数字艺术作品，将植物信号、环境数据与宇宙现象转化为沉浸式体验，激活公共空间并激发好奇心。UnCalculated Studio 曾参展 Ars Electronica、SIGGRAPH Los Angeles、ISEA2024、VIVID Sydney、SIGGRAPH Asia Brisbane & Daegu、布拉格四年展、桃园会展中心，以及墨尔本 Collingwood Yards 与 Federation Square 4K Digital Screen；他们以创新且开放的数字艺术实践著称，将社区与宇宙、以及周遭鲜活的生态连接起来。

Rewa 自 2012 年起即在混合现实中探索植物与算法，并拥有超过 25 年的动态图像、交互设计和数字环境经验。作为第一民族毛利艺术家（Ngai Tawake、Te Kaimaroke、Te Uri o Hau），她的作品将原住民知识与互动媒体编织在一起，并受到其在欧洲、亚洲与太平洋地区国际展示经验的滋养。Simon 是一位视听艺术家与音乐制作人，使用植物生物信号和实验材料创作定制化声音景观。他拥有奥克兰大学 Elam School of Art 的 MFA 学位；作为音乐人，他的作品在 YouTube 上累计观看量超过 4500 万，并曾与 Busta Rhymes、Popcaan、Wyclef Jean 等艺术家合作进入 Billboard 榜单。

description_en:
这件3D艺术作品《双生之树》将两棵形态各异的树木交织为一体，象征着香港科技大学清水湾校区与广州校区。

两个校区相辅相成、共生共荣，如同交错相依的树木，同心聚力，为港科大源源不断注入生机与活力。
description_cn:
Version 1 (Concise & Formal)

This 3D artwork Twin Trees depicts two different trees intertwined as a whole. It symbolizes the two campuses of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology: Clear Water Bay and Guangzhou.

The two campuses complement and nourish one another. Just like the interwoven trees, they unite closely to sustain the enduring vitality of HKUST.

Version 2 (Sleek & Artistic)

Named Twin Trees, this 3D piece presents two distinctive trees growing intricately together, representing HKUST’s Clear Water Bay and Guangzhou Campuses.

The two campuses thrive in mutual complementarity and interaction. Bound as one, they jointly fuel the university’s everlasting dynamism.
artist_bio_en:
Wenjing Mao is dedicated to exploring the intersection of art and technology. She is a digital visual creator and media interaction designer.

Yuxuan Chen is a young filmmaker and interdisciplinary visual artist with a background in Computer Science from The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

Yulin Yao is a visual artist specializing in surrealist aesthetics. Integrating psychology and philosophy into her practice, she creates narrative experiences that explore the inner mind and subconscious through immersive spatial design, interactive installations, and virtual reality (VR).

Shuyue Li is a digital artist, interaction designer, and researcher. Her work examines how digital media reshape human perception, spatial experience, and social connection, exploring the emotional relationships between people and their environments within the intertwined realms of the virtual and the real.

Hao Li is a media artist, researcher, and designer. His practice is grounded in a long-term exploration of media spaces, audiovisual art, and generative art, and has increasingly evolved toward the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and mixed reality (MR) as both artistic methodologies and research approaches.
artist_bio_cn:
毛雯婧，致力于艺术与科技的结合。数字视觉创作者，媒介交互设计师。

陈聿暄，青年导演、跨学科视觉艺术家，毕业于香港理工大学计算机专业。

姚钰琳。视觉艺术家。擅长超现实主义风格，作品融合心理学与哲学，通过沉浸式空间设计、交互装置与虚拟现实（VR），构建探索内在精神与潜意识的叙事体验。

李姝玥，数字艺术家、交互设计师与研究者。关注数字媒介如何重塑人类感知、空间体验与社会联结，探索虚拟与现实交织语境下人与环境的情感关系。

李昊，媒体艺术家、研究者及设计师，其创作基于对媒体空间、视听艺术与生成艺术的长期探索，并逐渐转向以AI与混合现实（MR）作为艺术方法与研究路径。

description_en:
If you were a butterfly, would you stop here?

This work is a collection of objects, furniture pieces, and habitat prototypes imagined for butterflies. Starting from the history of Buddleja, the migration of the Red Admiral butterfly, and the fictional story of Isabella Glanville, the project attempts to respond to non-human ways of sensing through design.

These objects exist somewhere between furniture, flowers, bodily organs, and architectural fragments. Some resemble landing points, some appear as glowing nests, while others suggest a bathroom, tower, chair, or temporary shelter made for butterflies. Rather than serving only human use, they imagine a space that might be chosen by another species through colour, light, scale, and form.

In this work, design becomes a form of invitation. It no longer focuses on controlling nature, but instead learns how to step back, attract, wait, and coexist. The Glanville Butterfly World therefore becomes a miniature world between an ecosystem, a dream, and a collection of objects.
description_cn:
如果你是蝴蝶，你会停下来吗？

这个作品是一组为蝴蝶想象的物件、家具与栖息原型。它以醉鱼草、红蛺蝶迁徙，以及虚构人物 Isabella Glanville 的故事为起点，尝试用设计回应非人类的感知方式。

这些物件介于家具、花朵、身体器官与建筑碎片之间。它们有的像降落点，有的像发光的巢穴，有的像为蝴蝶准备的浴室、塔、座椅或临时庇护所。它们不再只服务于人类的使用，而是试图从颜色、光线、尺度和形态上，想象一种“被另一个物种选择”的空间。

在这个作品中，设计成为一种邀请。它不再强调控制自然，而是学习如何退让、吸引、等待与共处。格兰维尔蝴蝶世界因此成为一个介于生态系统、梦境和物件收藏之间的微型世界。
artist_bio_en: I am an Year 4 architecture student at The Bartlett School of Architecture, UCL, with a strong interest in design, spatial storytelling, and material exploration. My work focuses on translating abstract ideas into clear and persuasive visual narratives, while balancing user needs, functionality, and design implementation. Alongside architecture, I am also a ceramic artist with my own kiln in London, exploring ceramics as both a creative practice and a form of material research.
artist_bio_cn: 我是伦敦大学学院巴特莱特建筑学院的大四建筑学生，对设计、空间叙事和材料探索有着浓厚兴趣。我的作品关注如何将抽象概念转化为清晰且具有说服力的视觉叙事，同时平衡使用者需求、功能性与设计落地。除了建筑学习之外，我也是一名陶瓷创作者，并在伦敦拥有自己的窑炉，将陶瓷作为一种创作实践和材料研究方式进行探索。

description_en: A soulmate-seeking journey through four symbolic spaces traces One’s transformation from incompleteness to self-realization, as they shed layers of desire, identity, and illusion to uncover the raw self within. The space shown is a lush rain forest based on Helen, where mushrooms act as genitalia, flowers as charm. Light and humidity blur boundaries between human and nature, self and desire. Generative AI is incorporated to facilitate texturing, modelling, and fast render previsualization.
description_cn: 这是一场穿梭于四个象征性空间的灵魂寻觅之旅，记录了One从残缺走向自我实现的蜕变历程——在层层剥离欲望、身份与幻象之后，最终显露出内在最原始、真实的自我。眼前呈现的空间是一片以“海伦”（Helen）为原型的繁茂雨林。在这里，蘑菇化作生殖的隐喻，花朵为魅惑的象征。氤氲的光影与潮湿的水汽交织，悄然消解了人与自然、自我与欲望之间的边界。生成式AI被用于辅助材质、建模以及渲染预览测试。
artist_bio_en: Axol is a media artist and a member of the Brat! studio, currently based between Suzhou and Hangzhou. Axol graduated from the Department of Aesthetics and Art Studies at the University of Tokyo. Their work often explores bodily narratives, with a visual language influenced by Japanese and French avant-garde theater and cult cinema. Working across AI, 3D, live-action film, XR, and theatrical media, They area currently engaged in both independent artistic practice and commercial AI-driven visual production. In 2026, their works were selected for or nominated by festivals and programs including FILE Festival, UFO Terminal, Fluxus Museum Prize, TapNow x SXSW, and Aranya Festival.
artist_bio_cn: 媒体艺术创作者和Brat!工作室的导演成员，现居于苏州和杭州。毕业于东京大学美学艺术学。作品常常触及身体叙事，视觉语言受日法先锋戏剧和邪典影像的影响，作品跨界AI、3D、实拍、XR、戏剧媒体，目前进行个人创作&商业广告影像AI制作。2026年入选及提名FILE Festival、UFO加载计划、Fluxus Museum Prize、Tapnow x SXSW、SURREALITY 2.0 HKUST、阿那亚戏剧节候鸟300等展览和奖项。

description_en:
In the development of modern technology, AI-generated natural plants are often based on decontextualized botanical datasets from the internet. The core critique of this work lies in exploring the data feeding bias of AI, and what kind of surreal digital plants AI will evolve when humans use extreme, artificial, and manipulated ecological scenes as the sole data source.

Black-box Photosynthesis is a MR installation that investigates how AI is not merely a production tool, but a critical medium to examine algorithmic bias and data ecology.

In nature, photosynthesis is the metabolic basis for plants to sustain life; however, in this work, the artist metaphorically regards AI algorithms as a source that provides digital photosynthesis, whose nutrients are not sunlight, but visual data input by humans, and whose opaque generation process borrows the concept of black box described by the computer science research field.

The project’s conceptual starting point is an original and experimental film shot on a Parisian rooftop: figures with animalistic horns navigating urban soil, while artificial paper flowers burn. This is not a ritual, but a constructed Anthropocene Edge-case Dataset. The surreal quality of the images stems from a highly compressed landscape of human anxiety. In the creation process, traditional botanical data was intentionally withheld from the AI. Instead, the AI was exclusively fed this contradictory video footage to generate 3D plant structures. Lacking biological context, the AI engaged in displaced learning: it misinterpreted the texture of paper as organic epidermis, the destructive act of burning as a blooming process, and the horn structures as botanical roots. The resulting MR exhibition places these AI-hallucinated mutated plant clusters featuring carbonized edges and skeletal stems, into the physical location.

By forcing the AI to digest human-curated scenes of ecological intervention rather than pure nature, the artwork poses a reflective question: If machine learning understands the natural world solely through humanity's fabricated and disruptive visual fragments, is the resulting digital ecology merely a cybernetic mirror of our own environmental alienation?
description_cn:
在现代技术的发展进程中，人工智能生成的自然植物往往依赖于互联网上脱离原真语境的植物学数据集。本作品的核心批判在于探索人工智能的投喂偏见（Data Feeding Bias）：当人类将极端、人造且经由操弄的生态场景作为唯一数据源时，人工智能会演化出怎样超现实的数字植被？

《黑箱光合》 是一件混合现实（MR）装置作品，它探讨了人工智能如何超越单纯的生产工具，转而成为审视算法偏见与数据生态的关键媒介。

在自然界中，光合作用是植物维持生命的代谢基础；然而在这件作品中，艺术家隐喻性地将人工智能算法视为提供“数字光合作用”的能量源，其养分并非阳光，而是人类输入的视觉数据；其不透明的生成过程则借用了计算机科学领域中的“黑箱（Black Box）”概念。

该项目的理念起点是一部在巴黎屋顶拍摄的原创实验影像：头长兽角的角色在城市土壤中穿行，人造纸花正在燃烧。这并非一场仪式，而是一个人工构建的“人类世边缘案例数据集（Anthropocene Edge-case Dataset）”。影像中超现实的特质，源于一种高度浓缩的人类焦虑景观。在创作过程中，艺术家刻意阻断了传统植物学数据的录入，转而仅向人工智能投喂这段充满矛盾性的视频素材，以此生成 3D 植物结构。

由于缺乏生物学语境的先验逻辑，人工智能进入了“错位学习（Displaced Learning）”状态：它将纸张纹理误认为有机表皮，将燃烧的破坏性行为误读为绽放过程，并将角状结构解析为植物根系。最终的 MR 展览将这些由人工智能“幻视”出的变异植株群簇，带有碳化的边缘和骨架般的茎干，置入物理空间之中。通过强迫人工智能去消化人类剪裁过的“生态干预”场景而非纯粹自然，最终作为一项基于研究的艺术作品，艺术家们追问：如果机器学习仅通过人类编造、割裂的视觉碎片来理解自然世界，那么由此产生的数字生态，是否仅仅是反映我们自身环境异化的一面控制论镜像？
artist_bio_en:
Joshua Nijiati Alimujiang is an artist and researcher currently based in Paris, operating at the intersection of extended cinematography, artificial intelligence, and digital anthropology. After earning an M.Phil. in Computational Media and Arts from HKUST (Guangzhou), he is currently a researcher at Sony Computer Science Laboratories (Sony CSL) and continuing his academic studies at École Polytechnique in France.

Peter Hanappe is a scientist-researcher with a PhD from the Institute IRCAM, who specializes in complex systems, artificial intelligence, and sustainability. He is widely recognized for developing open-source robotics and computational tools for micro-farming, striving to make decentralized, agroecological practices more resilient and environmentally efficient.

Rachel Armstrong is an architect and researcher of experimental architecture. She integrates synthetic biology into the built environment. She is renowned for advocating living architecture, designing buildings with organic, metabolic properties that can grow, self-repair, and sustainably interact with their ecological surroundings rather than merely extracting from them.

Caroline Hobkinson is an experimental food artist and conceptualist. She transforms gastronomy into multi-sensory performances. By combining culinary arts with neuroscience and anthropology, she designs immersive dining experiences that challenge perceptions of taste, texture, and ritual, turning everyday eating into a profound, interactive psychological exploration.

Eliza Calmat is an actress, director, and producer working between Paris and London. With a strong background in classical acting, she serves as artistic director for the immersive theater Neuf Sens. Her notable screen credits include the film Love is Blind and the television series Spiral.
artist_bio_cn:
Joshua Nijiati Alimujiang 是驻巴黎的艺术家和研究员，致力于人工智能、扩展电影和数字人类学的交叉领域研究。在获得香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术硕士学位后，他目前担任索尼计算机科学实验室（Sony CSL）的研究员，并在法国巴黎综合理工学院（École Polytechnique）继续深造。

Peter Hanappe 是一位拥有 IRCAM 研究所博士学位的Sony CSL科学家，专攻复杂系统、人工智能和可持续发展。他因开发用于微型农业的开源机器人和计算工具而闻名，致力于提升去中心化生态农业实践的韧性与环境效率。

Rachel Armstrong 是一位建筑师和实验建筑研究员。她将合成生物学融入建筑环境，并以倡导生命建筑（living architecture）而享誉建筑界。她设计的建筑具有有机的代谢特性，能够生长、自我修复，并与生态环境进行可持续的互动，而非仅仅从中索取资源。

Caroline Hobkinson 是一位实验艺术美食家和概念艺术家。她将美食转变为多感官的表演艺术。通过将烹饪艺术与神经科学、人类学相结合，她设计出各种沉浸式用餐体验，挑战人们对味道、质地和仪式的固有认知，将日常饮食转化为一种深刻的、互动式的心理探索。

Eliza Calmat是一位活跃于巴黎和伦敦之间的演员、导演和制片人。凭借深厚的古典表演背景，她担任沉浸式剧团 Neuf Sens 的艺术总监。她的代表作包括电影《盲爱》（Love is Blind）和电视剧《螺旋》（Spiral）。

description_en:
Cloud of the Seasons is a new augmented reality iteration of Seasons, an immersive project that explores emotional and psychological cycles through evolving digital environments. While the original work unfolds through a physical display, this new version replaces the screen with a monumental virtual cloud that appears within public space through AR, creating a shared, site-responsive experience.

This cloud is composed of a series of generative visual compositions developed for each season—spring, summer, autumn, and winter—each embodying distinct emotional states, textures, and color dynamics. These visual elements are not fixed: they are continuously generated and altered through real-time weather data, allowing the work to evolve in direct dialogue with its environment.

Artificial intelligence and generative systems play a central role in shaping these transformations, modulating visual behaviors, transitions, and atmospheric qualities. The cloud becomes a living entity unstable, reactive, and ephemeral mirroring both climatic variations and inner emotional landscapes.

By merging natural data flows with artificial processes, Cloud of the Seasons questions our relationship to environment, perception, and temporality. It creates a space where external conditions and internal states intertwine, offering a contemplative and sensory experience that shifts over time.

Situated between public art, immersive media, and experimental narrative, the project proposes a new way of inhabiting digital forms in physical space transforming the sky itself into a mutable, poetic interface.
description_cn:
《Cloud of the Seasons》是《Seasons》的全新增强现实版本；原作是一项通过不断演化的数字环境探索情感与心理周期的沉浸式项目。原作通过物理显示屏展开，而这一新版本则以 AR 中出现在公共空间的纪念碑式虚拟云取代屏幕，创造出一种共享的、与场地相互响应的体验。

这朵云由一系列为春、夏、秋、冬四季发展出的生成式视觉构成组成，每一季都承载不同的情绪状态、纹理与色彩动态。这些视觉元素并非固定不变，而是通过实时天气数据持续生成与改变，使作品与其所处环境展开直接对话。

人工智能与生成系统在塑造这些变化中发挥核心作用，调节视觉行为、过渡方式与氛围品质。云成为一种不稳定、可反应、转瞬即逝的生命体，同时映照气候变化与内在情绪景观。

通过将自然数据流与人工过程结合，《Cloud of the Seasons》追问我们与环境、感知和时间性的关系。它创造了一个外部条件与内在状态彼此交织的空间，提供一种随时间移动而变化的沉思性、感官性体验。

项目位于公共艺术、沉浸式媒体与实验叙事之间，提出一种在物理空间中栖居数字形态的新方式，将天空本身转化为可变的、诗意的界面。
artist_bio_en:
Arnaud Laffond is a French multidisciplinary artist whose work explores the relationships between perception, memory, and immersive digital environments. At the crossroads of installation, video, and interactive experiences, he develops evocative works where light, color, and digital matter become spaces to inhabit.

His projects question states of consciousness, personal narratives, and the transformations of reality through immersive devices, informed by research blending science, fiction, and sensory experience. He is particularly interested in the links between trauma, imagination, and reconstruction, creating hybrid narrative forms that bridge contemporary art and new audiovisual forms of expression.

His work has been presented in several international contexts dedicated to new immersive forms, notably at markets and festivals such as NewImages, GIFF, and the Venice Film Festival (Venice Immersive), where he is currently developing virtual reality projects.

Among them, Seasons is an interactiv and generativ work produced by Art Explora and It Is Now, with development by Edgar Schuban, exploring emotional cycles through a sensory and poetic experience.

Arnaud Laffond continues to develop projects at the intersection of immersive art, experimental storytelling, and large-scale participatory installations.
artist_bio_cn:
Arnaud Laffond 是一位法国跨媒介艺术家，其作品探索感知、记忆与沉浸式数字环境之间的关系。在装置、影像与互动体验的交汇处，他发展出富有召唤力的作品，使光、色彩与数字物质成为可以被栖居的空间。

他的项目通过沉浸式装置追问意识状态、个人叙事与现实的转化，并受到融合科学、虚构与感官经验的研究启发。他尤其关注创伤、想象与重构之间的联系，创造出连接当代艺术与新型视听表达的混合叙事形式。

他的作品曾在多个关注沉浸式新形式的国际语境中呈现，尤其包括 NewImages、GIFF 与威尼斯电影节 Venice Immersive 等市场和电影节；他目前也在持续开发虚拟现实项目。

其中，《Seasons》是一件由 Art Explora 与 It Is Now 出品、Edgar Schuban 参与开发的互动生成作品，通过感官性、诗意化的体验探索情感周期。

Arnaud Laffond 持续在沉浸式艺术、实验叙事与大型参与式装置的交汇处发展新的项目。

description_en:
Bug in My Software (BIMS) is a real-time simulation paired with handmade textile installation that reimagines artificial intelligence along the biological, cultural, and industrial history of silk production. The project is centered on the silkmoth (Bombyx mori), one of the earliest lifeforms redesigned by human intervention. In BIMS, silkmoth DNA, reproductive cycle, and labor role become the blueprint for a real-time synthetic ecosystem populated by evolving digital agents. Situating AI within the history of textile labor, biological engineering, and industrial automation, BIMS reframes machine intelligence as collective, biological, and materially entangled.

The system runs as a continuously evolving simulation in which artificial silkmoths inhabit, mutate, adapt to, and interact with each other and their simulated speculative ecosystem. The visual environment behaves as a hybrid between an ecological terrarium and a computational substrate, in which digital organisms evolve over long-form interaction cycles. This ecology does not respond to discrete user commands: rather than consumption of a user-controlled interface, the installation frames the viewing experience as “field observation” of a xenobiological AI.

Beyond simulation, the project includes a material archive: hand-woven textile encoding real silkmoth DNA sequences placed on the floor. The textile serves as a symbolic dataset - palimpsest of human intervention into the species - with the patterns informing the visual grammar of the simulation.

Though the textile’s design is informed by converting DNA sequence into a visual color-coded field via algorithmic processes, its materiality and construction are the result of manual, repetitive labor, performed by the artist over several months. This
juxtaposition of handcraft and computational automation highlights the dynamics of hidden labor behind both traditional and digital production systems.

Lastly, BIMS reframes the immersive experience as an embodied physical encounter, as the visitors are invited to engage with the textile, to sit, recline, embed (or re-embed) themselves into the speculative ecosystem while contemplating its digital landscape.
description_cn:
《Bug in my Software》（BIMS）是一件实时模拟与手工织物装置相结合的作品，从丝绸生产的生物、文化与工业历史出发重新想象人工智能。项目以家蚕蛾（Bombyx mori）为中心，它是最早被人类干预并重新设计的生命形式之一。在 BIMS 中，蚕蛾的 DNA、繁殖周期与劳动角色成为实时合成生态系统的蓝本，系统中栖居着不断演化的数字主体。作品将 AI 置于纺织劳动、生物工程与工业自动化的历史之中，重新将机器智能理解为一种集体性的、生物性的、与物质纠缠在一起的存在。

系统作为持续演化的模拟运行，人工蚕蛾在其中栖息、变异、适应，并与彼此及其推想生态系统互动。视觉环境介于生态玻璃缸与计算基底之间，数字生物在长时段互动周期中持续演化。这一生态并不响应离散的用户指令：装置并非提供一个可被用户控制和消费的界面，而是将观看经验设定为对异种生物学 AI 的“田野观察”。

除模拟之外，项目还包含一份物质档案：铺设在地面的手工编织织物，其中编码了真实蚕蛾 DNA 序列。织物作为一个象征性数据集，也是一层关于人类对物种干预的重写文本，其图案影响着模拟的视觉语法。

尽管织物设计来自将 DNA 序列通过算法过程转化为色彩编码的视觉场，但其材料性与制作过程则源于艺术家数月中重复的手工劳动。手工技艺与计算自动化之间的并置，凸显了传统与数字生产系统背后隐藏劳动的动态关系。

最后，BIMS 将沉浸式体验重新理解为一种具身的物理遭遇：观众被邀请与织物互动，坐下、躺下，将自己嵌入或重新嵌入这一推想生态系统之中，同时凝视其数字景观。
artist_bio_en:
Alina Nazmeeva is a Tatarstan-born media artist, designer and educator working across physical installation, digital simulation, textile, and XR. With these diverse media, her practice builds complex worlds that investigate how technologies - emerging and established - shape, and are shaped by, situated spatial, social, and ecological practices.
Her work has been exhibited internationally, including at the Venice Biennale of Architecture, the Architecture + Design Museum in Los Angeles, the Beall Center for Art + Technology, and in major art and design festivals such as DA Z (Zurich), Slamdance (Los Angeles), HKWalls (Hong Kong), Collectible NYC, Collectible Brussels, and Alcova Milano. She has presented at Harvard GSD, UMPRUM, Parsons, Shanghai Institute of Visual Art, Seoul National University, Duke University, SIGGRAPH and ISEA. Her writing has appeared in Plat, Voices (Towards Other Institutions), Media-N, and AD (forthcoming).
Alina is Assistant Professor of Computation at the Illinois School of Architecture at UIUC. She holds a Master’s degree from MIT SA+P and has held fellowships at the University of Michigan (2022–24), the Canadian Centre for Architecture (2022), and the Strelka Institute (2017). She has held residencies at Art OMI & Monira Foundation (ongoing).
artist_bio_cn:
Alina Nazmeeva 是出生于鞑靼斯坦的媒体艺术家、设计师与教育者，实践横跨实体装置、数字模拟、织物与 XR。通过这些多样媒介，她建构复杂的世界，研究新兴与既有技术如何塑造、也如何被特定空间、社会与生态实践所塑造。

她的作品曾在国际范围内展出，包括威尼斯建筑双年展、洛杉矶 Architecture + Design Museum、Beall Center for Art + Technology，以及 DA Z（苏黎世）、Slamdance（洛杉矶）、HKWalls（香港）、Collectible NYC、Collectible Brussels、Alcova Milano 等重要艺术与设计节。她曾在 Harvard GSD、UMPRUM、Parsons、上海视觉艺术学院、首尔国立大学、杜克大学、SIGGRAPH 与 ISEA 发表和展示作品。她的写作发表于 Plat、Voices (Towards Other Institutions)、Media-N，并即将发表于 AD。

Alina 现任 UIUC Illinois School of Architecture 计算方向助理教授。她拥有 MIT SA+P 硕士学位，并曾获密歇根大学（2022-24）、加拿大建筑中心（2022）和 Strelka Institute（2017）研究资助；她也持续担任 Art OMI & Monira Foundation 驻留艺术家。

description_en:
Kandinsky at HKUST(GZ) is a mixed reality (MR) and AI-powered work that reimagines the legacy of abstract art pioneer Wassily Kandinsky. In a quiet corner of the HKUST(GZ) campus, Kandinsky steps across time, brush never still, as he re-paints the surrounding scenery in his iconic abstract style — now fused with the fluid gestures of ink wash art. It is a convergence of artistic soul and algorithmic perception.

When a viewer approaches, Kandinsky’s reflections on art resonate through the air, while his classic compositions slowly float out from his figure, forming a flowing, open-air museum. With technology as its bridge, this piece invites a heartfelt dialogue between a century-old avant-garde spirit and a contemporary campus — a tribute to HKUST(GZ) as a fertile ground for innovation, where art and science have never been apart.
description_cn: 《康定斯基在校园》是一件以混合现实（MR）与AI技术重构抽象艺术大师康定斯基的作品。在校园一角，康定斯基踏过时光，执笔不息，以他标志性的抽象风格融合水墨艺术重绘眼前的校园景致，是艺术灵魂与算法感知的共融。当发现观众时，康定斯基的对艺术的理解将在空中回响，他的经典作品亦缓缓漂浮而出，构筑一座流动的空中美术馆。作品以科技为桥梁，让百年前的先锋艺术与当代校园深情对话，致敬港科广作为创新沃土的精神——艺术与科学，从未分离。

description_en:
Enchanted Arbor explores how sculpture can intervene in physical space in a gentle and poetic manner, evoking a magical, mysterious, and imaginative atmosphere within everyday environments. Rather than dominating its surroundings, the work subtly reshapes viewers’ perceptions of nature, ornament, and digital media through a surreal visual language. It draws inspiration from Professor David Yip’s Cinematic Surrealism 1.0, the formal aesthetics of traditional Chinese bonsai and scholar’s rocks, and Wallace Chan’s integration of sculptural imagination, gem-like materiality, and poetic transformation.
At the center is a tree-like form surrounded by flowing lines inspired by auspicious cloud motifs, suggesting breath, circulation, and invisible energy. The surfaces of the trunk and base are animated with shifting surrealist color blocks. Resembling dreamlike reflections, mineral textures, and streams of consciousness, these colors move, overlap, and reorganize across the sculptural form. The dynamic materials transform the sculpture from a static object into a living presence that appears to breathe and renew itself. The cloud-like lines extend through space with a restrained rhythm, reinforcing a sense of fluidity and suspension.
AI supports early-stage concept generation and visual exploration, while also contributing to the randomized generation of trunk forms and leaf distribution. Combined with procedural methods, this process allows the natural forms to emerge through an interplay of rules and contingency rather than directly replicating real plants. The work is procedurally modeled and dynamically designed in Houdini, textured in Substance Painter, and presented in real time in Unity. By interweaving cultural memory, natural symbolism, and contemporary digital aesthetics, Enchanted Arbor proposes a surreal spatial poetics rooted in Eastern aesthetics and oriented toward future media experiences.
description_cn:
《幻木栖云》探索雕塑如何以温和而诗意的方式介入物理空间，并在日常环境中唤起一种魔幻、神秘而富有想象力的氛围。作品并不试图占据或支配周围空间，而是借助超现实的视觉语言，细腻地改变观众对自然、装饰与数字媒介之间关系的感知。其创作受到叶纪文教授“电影超现实主义 1.0”、中国传统盆景与赏石美学，以及 Wallace Chan 作品中雕塑想象、宝石质感与诗性转化的启发。
作品以一棵树状形态为核心，祥云般的流动线条围绕枝干延展，暗示气息、循环与无形能量。树干与底座表面覆盖着持续变化的超现实主义色块动画：色彩如同梦境中的光影、矿物纹理与流动意识，不断在形体表面迁移、交叠与重组。动态材质使雕塑不再只是静止的物体，而更像处于缓慢呼吸和自我更新中的生命体。祥云线条以轻盈而克制的视觉节奏穿梭于空间之中，与树状结构彼此呼应，进一步强化了作品中流动、漂浮的感受。
在创作过程中，AI 不仅用于早期概念生成与视觉启发，也参与树干形态和树叶分布的随机生成。通过 AI 辅助生成与程序化方法的结合，作品中的自然形态并非对现实植物的直接复制，而是在规则与偶然之间持续生长。树干的分叉、树叶的位置以及整体结构中的细微差异共同构成了一种具有生命感的非重复性。最终作品通过 Houdini 进行程序化建模与动态设计，在 Substance Painter 中完成材质制作，并于 Unity 中实现实时呈现。作品将传统文化记忆、自然象征与当代数字视觉语言交织在一起，尝试构建一种既根植东方美学，又面向未来媒介体验的超现实空间诗学。
artist_bio_en:
The artist team is led by Professor David Kei Man Yip from the Computational Media and Arts Thrust at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou). Professor Yip is an educator, researcher, and artist whose work explores the intersection of technology and storytelling in creative media. With a background spanning cinematic media production, animation, interactive entertainment, and practice-based research, he investigates how emerging digital tools can reshape media form, creative content, and artistic experience. He is currently an Assistant Professor at HKUST(GZ) and Director of the Computational Media and Arts Lab, where he leads the Creative Art Tech (CAT) team.

The team also includes two members of the CAT team: Research Assistant Zheyu Fu and PhD student Yuelu Li. Zheyu Fu’s research and creative practice focus on immersive visual presentation and digital media art. Drawing on Eastern aesthetics and philosophical thinking, his work explores poetic expressions of digital media between order and contingency, seeking to create a dialogue between technological logic and Eastern perceptual experience. Yuelu Li is a PhD student in Computational Media and Arts at HKUST(GZ), supervised by Professor David Kei Man Yip and Professor Cheuk Yi Kelvin Yuen. Her research focuses on AI-driven storytelling, including interactive narrative systems and AI-mediated storytelling practices on social media platforms.
artist_bio_cn:
该艺术家团队由香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术学域的叶纪文教授带领。叶教授是一位教育者、研究者与艺术家，长期探索技术与叙事在创意媒体中的交叉关系。他的背景横跨电影媒体制作、动画、互动娱乐与实践型研究，关注新兴数字工具如何重塑媒介形式、创意内容与艺术体验。Yip 教授现任香港科技大学（广州）助理教授、计算媒体与艺术实验室主任，并带领 Creative Art Tech（CAT）团队开展相关研究与创作。

团队成员包括 CAT 团队中的两位成员：研究助理傅哲宇与博士生李玥璐。傅哲宇是香港科技大学（广州）CAT 团队研究助理，其研究与创作实践聚焦于沉浸式视觉呈现与数字媒体艺术。他的工作借鉴东方美学与哲学思考，探索数字媒体在秩序与偶然之间的诗性表达，并试图在技术逻辑与东方感知经验之间建立对话。李玥璐是香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术方向博士生，由叶纪文教授与袁卓尔教授共同指导，同时也是 CAT 团队成员。其研究关注 AI 驱动叙事，包括互动叙事系统，以及社交媒体平台中的 AI 介导叙事实践。

description_en: Eduardo Kac的代表作《GFP Bunny》，是生物艺术史上最具标志性的作品之一。作品以名为 Alba 的绿色荧光兔为核心，将基因工程、生命伦理、公众讨论与艺术创作交织在一起，成为生物技术进入当代艺术语境的重要里程碑。这只曾出现在《生活大爆炸》《神探夏洛克》《辛普森一家》等流行文化语境中的转基因兔，也将在此次展览中以全新的形式再次呈现。
description_cn: **Eduardo Kac’s iconic work *GFP Bunny* is widely regarded as one of the most influential and emblematic artworks in the history of bio art. Centered on a genetically modified green fluorescent rabbit named *Alba*, the project intertwines genetic engineering, bioethics, public discourse, and artistic practice, marking a significant milestone in the integration of biotechnology into contemporary art. This transgenic rabbit—referenced in popular culture through works such as *The Big Bang Theory*, *Sherlock*, and *The Simpsons*—will be reintroduced in a new form as part of this exhibition.**
artist_bio_en: Eduardo Kac is internationally recognized for his groundbreaking work in contemporary art and poetry. In the early 1980s, Kac created digital, holographic and online works that anticipated the global culture we live in today, composed of ever-changing information in constant flux. In 1997 the artist coined the term "Bio Art," igniting the development of this new art form with works such as his transgenic rabbit GFP Bunny (2000) and Natural History of the Enigma (2009), which earned him the Golden Nica, the most prestigious award in the field of media art. GFP Bunny has become a global phenomenon, having been appropriated by major popular culture franchises such as Sherlock, Big Bang Theory and Simpsons, and by writers such as Margaret Atwood and Michael Crichton. In 2017, Kac created Inner Telescope, a work conceived for and realized in outer space with the cooperation of French astronaut Thomas Pesquet. In 2024, Kac's Ágora flew to deep space aboard the Centaur rocket and is now in a perpetual heliocentric orbit. Kac's Adsum landed on the Moon in 2025. Kac’s singular and highly influential career spans poetry, performance, drawing, printmaking, photography, artist's books, early digital and online works, holography, telepresence, bio art, and space art. Kac has also authored or edited several books, including Telepresence and Bio Art -- Networking Humans, Rabbits and Robots (University of Michigan Press, 2005). Kac’s work has been exhibited internationally at venues such as New Museum, New York; Pompidou Center, Paris; MAXXI-Museum of XXI Century Arts, Rome; Mori Art Museum, Tokyo; Reina Sofia Museum, Madrid; Power Station of Art, Shanghai; and Seoul Museum of Art, Korea. Kac's work has been showcased in biennials such as Venice Biennale, Italy; Yokohama Triennial, Japan; Gwangju Biennale, Korea; Bienal de Sao Paulo, Brazil; and Bienal de Habana, Cuba. His works are in major collections such as Museum of Modern Art-MoMA, New York; The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York; Tate Modern, London; Reina Sofia Museum, Madrid; Victoria & Albert Museum, London; Museum Les Abattoirs—Frac Occitanie Toulouse, France; Valencian Institute of Modern Art-IVAM, Spain; Museum ZKM, Karlsruhe, Germany; and Museum of Contemporary Art of São Paulo, among others.
artist_bio_cn: Eduardo Kac 因其在当代艺术与诗歌领域的开创性实践而享誉国际。20 世纪 80 年代初，Kac 创作了数字、全息与网络作品，预示了我们今天所处的全球文化：一个由不断变化、持续流动的信息构成的世界。1997 年，他提出“Bio Art”（生物艺术）一词，并以转基因兔子《GFP Bunny》（2000）和《Natural History of the Enigma》（2009）等作品推动这一新艺术形式的发展；后者为他赢得了媒体艺术领域最具声望的奖项 Golden Nica。《GFP Bunny》已成为全球文化现象，被《Sherlock》《The Big Bang Theory》《The Simpsons》等大众文化作品，以及 Margaret Atwood、Michael Crichton 等作家借用和引用。2017 年，Kac 创作了《Inner Telescope》，这是一件为外太空构想并在法国宇航员 Thomas Pesquet 协助下实现的作品。2024 年，Kac 的《Ágora》搭乘 Centaur 火箭飞向深空，目前处于永久日心轨道。Kac 的《Adsum》于 2025 年登陆月球。Kac 独特而极具影响力的艺术生涯横跨诗歌、表演、绘画、版画、摄影、艺术家书、早期数字与网络作品、全息术、远程临场、生物艺术和太空艺术。他还著有或编辑多本书籍，包括《Telepresence and Bio Art -- Networking Humans, Rabbits and Robots》（University of Michigan Press，2005）。Kac 的作品曾在纽约 New Museum、巴黎蓬皮杜中心、罗马 MAXXI、东京森美术馆、马德里 Reina Sofia Museum、上海当代艺术博物馆、韩国首尔美术馆等国际机构展出，并曾亮相威尼斯双年展、横滨三年展、光州双年展、圣保罗双年展和哈瓦那双年展。他的作品被纽约现代艺术博物馆 MoMA、纽约大都会艺术博物馆、伦敦 Tate Modern、马德里 Reina Sofia Museum、伦敦 Victoria & Albert Museum、法国 Les Abattoirs—Frac Occitanie Toulouse、西班牙 Valencian Institute of Modern Art-IVAM、德国 ZKM 以及圣保罗当代艺术博物馆等重要收藏机构收藏。

description_en:
Timemachine Love is inspired by a widely circulated verse:
"I love three things in this world. Sun, moon and you. Sun for morning, moon for night, and you forever."
The installation brings together the structural logic of the Chinese armillary sphere, the Cardan incense burner, and the modern mechanical clock to create a dynamic cosmos centered on time and love. Its form is derived from the infinity symbol (∞), unfolding through continuous cycles of rotation and repetition. The Chinese armillary sphere's vision of cosmic order, the dynamic balance embodied by the Cardan Incense Burner, and the human conception of time represented by the clock converge within a single structure, where time is understood not as a linear sequence of measured moments, but as an ongoing process of recurrence, continuity, and transformation. At the center of the work, a pulsating heart remains balanced within these revolving structures, serving as a symbol of emotional bonds that endure through time and change.
By combining traditional Chinese cosmology with contemporary digital art, Timemachine Love explores the relationship between time and human affection. The work presents love as a force that transcends memory, distance, and time itself. Like the recurring movement of celestial bodies and the alternation of day and night, love becomes part of a larger cycle—one that continues beyond individual moments and resonates within the infinite flow of time.
description_cn:
《Timemachine Love》的创作灵感源于一句广为流传的诗句：
“浮世三千，吾爱有三。日月与卿。日为朝，月为暮，卿为朝朝暮暮。”
作品将浑天仪、被中香炉与现代机械钟表的结构逻辑融为一体，构建出一个围绕时间与爱的动态宇宙。整体造型源于无限符号（∞），通过持续旋转与循环往复的运动不断展开。浑天仪所象征的宇宙秩序、被中香炉所体现的动态平衡，以及钟表所承载的人类时间观在同一结构中交汇，使时间不再只是被丈量的刻度，而成为一个不断循环、延续与演化的过程。位于装置中心的脉动之心在循环往复的轨道之间保持动态平衡，象征情感连接在时间流动中的延续与共鸣。
通过将中国传统宇宙观与当代数字艺术语言相结合，《Timemachine Love》试图探讨时间与情感之间的关系。作品将爱呈现为一种能够穿越记忆、距离与岁月的力量。如同星辰运行、昼夜更替一般，爱成为更宏大循环的一部分——超越个体生命中的短暂瞬间，在无限流动的时间长河之中持续回响，并获得永恒。
artist_bio_en: Shuyue Li is a digital artist, designer and researcher based at the Center for Metaverse and Computational Creativity (MC²), HKUST (Guangzhou). She earned her MA in Digital Direction from the Royal College of Art and BA in Digital Media Art from Beihang University. Rooted in human-computer interaction (HCI), her research explores how emerging technologies restructure human spatial perception, affective engagement and human-environment relations across physical-virtual divides. Her artistic practice employs XR, AI and immersive media to craft experiential works that dissolve the line between reality and imagination.

研究立足人机交互（HCI），探究前沿技术对人类感知、社交联结的重构逻辑，依托 XR、AIGC 与交互系统，深耕混合现实的临场感、具身交互与情感交互机制；艺术创作聚焦 3D 艺术、VR/AR 及沉浸式媒介，围绕虚实场域的边界演变，探索数字技术重构空间认知、人与环境情感联结的创新路径。

title_cn: 算法 AI 数字艺术 2026
description_en:
Algorithms is an AI-generated immersive artwork that explores the convergence of human cognition and artificial intelligence. Inspired by advances in brain-computer interfaces, neural networks, and machine learning, the work imagines a future where the boundaries between biological and digital intelligence become increasingly fluid.

Created using generative AI models, Algorithms visualizes speculative environments that reflect the flow of information between the human mind and intelligent systems. The work explores how AI is transforming creativity, perception, memory, and decision-making, while questioning what it means to think, create, and imagine in collaboration with machines. Through a process of prompting, iteration, and curation, artificial intelligence becomes both the medium and the subject of the work.

The imagery presents dreamlike landscapes where neural pathways, data streams, and organic forms merge into hybrid worlds that blur distinctions between human consciousness and computational intelligence. These visual narratives draw upon contemporary research into cognitive enhancement, neural interfaces, and emerging technologies that seek to expand human capabilities through direct interaction with AI systems.

Rather than portraying artificial intelligence as a replacement for human creativity, Algorithms explores the potential for symbiosis between human intuition and machine intelligence. It asks how future generations may learn, communicate, and create when cognition is increasingly augmented by intelligent technologies. At the same time, the work encourages reflection on the ethical and philosophical implications of this transformation, including questions of agency, autonomy, and identity.

By harnessing AI as a creative collaborator, Algorithms offers a speculative vision of a future shaped by human-machine partnership. The work invites audiences to consider both the opportunities and challenges of an increasingly interconnected world, where creativity emerges from the dynamic exchange between natural and artificial forms of intelligence.
description_cn:
《算法》是一件由 AI 生成的沉浸式艺术作品，探索人类认知与人工智能的汇合。作品受到脑机接口、神经网络和机器学习发展的启发，想象一个生物智能与数字智能边界日益流动的未来。

作品使用生成式 AI 模型创作，视觉化反映人类心智与智能系统之间信息流动的推想环境。它探索 AI 如何改变创造力、感知、记忆与决策，同时追问与机器协作进行思考、创作和想象意味着什么。在提示、迭代与策展的过程中，人工智能既成为作品媒介，也成为作品主题。

影像呈现出梦境般的景观，神经路径、数据流与有机形态融合为混合世界，模糊人类意识与计算智能之间的区分。这些视觉叙事借鉴了关于认知增强、神经接口以及通过与 AI 系统直接互动来扩展人类能力的新兴技术研究。

《算法》并不将人工智能描绘为人类创造力的替代者，而是探索人类直觉与机器智能之间共生的可能。它提出问题：当认知越来越多地被智能技术增强，未来世代将如何学习、沟通和创造？与此同时，作品也鼓励观众反思这一转变的伦理与哲学含义，包括能动性、自主性与身份等问题。

通过将 AI 作为创意协作者，《算法》提出一种由人机伙伴关系塑造的推想未来。作品邀请观众同时思考一个日益互联的世界所带来的机遇与挑战，在那里，创造力从自然智能与人工智能之间的动态交换中涌现。
artist_bio_en:
Kadine James is a British multidisciplinary artist, curator, and immersive storyteller working at the forefront of artificial intelligence, augmented reality, virtual worlds, and digital culture. Her practice explores the evolving relationship between humanity and technology, using emerging tools to create poetic, speculative, and emotionally resonant experiences that challenge traditional notions of identity, creativity, and presence.

Drawing from fashion, cinema, gaming, and contemporary art, James creates immersive works that exist across physical and digital spaces. Through AI-generated imagery, moving image, spatial computing, and interactive experiences, she investigates themes of transformation, memory, embodiment, and collective futures. Her work often centres on the digital self—examining how avatars, synthetic media, and machine intelligence are reshaping the ways we express, represent, and understand ourselves.

As Founder and Artistic Director of The Immersive KIND, James has spent the last decade developing pioneering projects that bridge art, technology, and culture. Her works have been exhibited internationally and presented at museums, galleries, film festivals, fashion weeks, and technology conferences, reaching audiences across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and North America. She has collaborated with leading cultural institutions, universities, and global brands to explore new forms of creative expression enabled by AI and immersive technologies.

Central to James's practice is a belief that technology can be used not only as a tool, but as a creative collaborator. Her work embraces experimentation and world-building, creating dreamlike environments that invite audiences to reflect on the possibilities and complexities of an increasingly hybrid future. Through immersive installations, AI-generated narratives, and augmented experiences, she explores how emerging technologies can expand artistic language while remaining deeply connected to human emotion and imagination.

For this exhibition, James presents a body of work that explores the convergence of artificial intelligence and immersive media, inviting viewers into liminal spaces where reality, memory, and machine imagination intertwine. Her work offers a vision of the future that is both critical and hopeful—one in which technology becomes a catalyst for new forms of creativity, connection, and wonder.
artist_bio_cn:
Kadine James 是英国跨媒介艺术家、策展人和沉浸式叙事创作者，工作位于人工智能、增强现实、虚拟世界与数字文化的前沿。她的实践探索人类与技术之间不断演变的关系，使用新兴工具创造诗意的、推想性的、富有情感共鸣的体验，挑战关于身份、创造力与临场的传统观念。

James 从时尚、电影、游戏与当代艺术中汲取灵感，创作跨越物理与数字空间的沉浸式作品。通过 AI 生成图像、动态图像、空间计算与互动体验，她研究转化、记忆、具身性与集体未来等主题。她的作品常以数字自我为核心，考察化身、合成媒体与机器智能如何重塑我们表达、再现和理解自身的方式。

作为 The Immersive KIND 的创始人与艺术总监，James 在过去十年中持续发展连接艺术、技术与文化的先锋项目。她的作品曾在国际范围展出，并于博物馆、画廊、电影节、时装周和技术会议中呈现，触达欧洲、亚洲、中东和北美的观众。她曾与重要文化机构、大学和全球品牌合作，探索 AI 与沉浸式技术所开启的新型创意表达。

James 实践的核心信念是，技术不仅可以作为工具，也可以成为创意协作者。她的作品拥抱实验与世界建构，创造梦境般的环境，邀请观众反思日益混合的未来所蕴含的可能性与复杂性。通过沉浸式装置、AI 生成叙事和增强体验，她探索新兴技术如何拓展艺术语言，同时仍与人类情感和想象保持深刻连接。

在本次展览中，James 呈现一组探索人工智能与沉浸式媒体交汇的作品，邀请观众进入现实、记忆与机器想象相互交织的阈限空间。她的作品提出一种既批判又充满希望的未来图景：技术成为新创造力、新连接与新奇迹的催化剂。

description_en:
One Who Deviates does not attempt to draw conclusions about existence or meaning, but rather constructs a space for individuals to dwell and reflect. Here, action, order, and structure are presented as a state of continuous operation, with the core focus of the work being how the individual perceives their position within it.

The imagery and spatial relationships in the work do not point toward a specific narrative; rather, they appear as fragments suspended between progression and stagnation, recurring repeatedly yet leading to no destination. Through this undefined state, One Who Deviates proposes a possibility: that moving forward does not necessarily imply direction, and participation is not synonymous with understanding.

Within this field, order and imbalance coexist; the acts of watching and being watched, following and choosing, constantly intersect. The work does not emphasize conflict or opposition, but allows these states to exist naturally, enabling the audience to gradually become aware of their own feelings and reactions within the space.

One Who Deviates does not demand judgment or identification from the audience; instead, it invites them to temporarily set aside expectations of results and meaning, to linger in the space, and to listen to the intuition of the body and the hesitations within. Meaning is not directly bestowed by external structures or collective behavior, but is generated through the individual's continuous process of awareness, deviation, and repositioning.
description_cn:
偏离者| One Who Deviates 并不试图给出关于存在或意义的结论，而是构建一个供个体停留与思考的空间。在这里，行动、秩序与结构被呈现为一种持续运作的状态，而个体如何在其中感知自身位置，成为作品所关注的核心。

作品中的形象与空间关系不指向具体叙事，它们更像是处于前行与停滞之间的片段，反复出现却不通向终点。通过这种未被明确指向的状态，偏离者提出一种可能性：前进并不必然意味着方向，参与也不等同于理解。

在这一场域中，秩序与失衡并行存在，观看与被观看、跟随与选择不断交错。作品并未强调冲突或对立，而是让这些状态自然共存，使观众逐渐意识到自身在其中的感受与反应。

偏离者并不要求观众作出判断或认同，而是邀请其暂时放下对结果与意义的期待，在空间中停留，倾听身体的直觉与内在的犹豫。意义并非由外部结构或集体行为直接赋予，而是在个体不断觉察、偏离与重新定位的过程中生成。
artist_bio_en:
Yulin Yao is a visual artist and digital art creator active between Europe and Asia. She is currently pursuing a PhD at the Computational Media and Arts (CMA) at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou).

Her work is characterized by dreamlike, surreal visual language, often infused with symbolic structures and the sensory experiences rooted in Eastern cultural contexts. Her practice spans immersive experience design, interactive installations, and virtual reality works. Her works have been exhibited at Dutch Design Week, Kaboom Animation Festival, and other major art and design platforms across Europe.

At this stage, she has begun to integrate psychological perspectives and human-computer interaction (HCI) technologies into her artistic practice, exploring how biosignals such as EEG can capture unspoken emotions and inner perceptions. She focuses on the body's responses and psychological states of individuals within immersive environments, seeking to create a more sensitive and empathetic mode of interaction within digital spaces.

She believes that technology is not merely a tool, but can also become an extension of perception. By navigating digital spaces that hover between reality and fiction, her work invites viewers into a quieter, more introspective state of seeing, where, through the subtle interplay of image, space, and body, they may rediscover a sense of themselves.
artist_bio_cn:
姚钰琳（Yulin Yao）是一位活跃于欧洲与亚洲的视觉艺术家与数字艺术创作者，现于香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术学域（CMA）攻读博士学位。

她的创作以梦境般、超现实的视觉语言为特征，常融入象征性结构与东方文化语境中的感性经验。作品涵盖沉浸式体验设计、交互装置与虚拟现实作品，曾在荷兰设计周（Dutch Design Week）、Kaboom动画节等多个欧洲重要艺术与设计平台展出。

在现阶段，她开始尝试将心理学视角与人机交互（HCI）技术融入艺术创作，探索如何通过脑电（EEG）等生物信号捕捉那些难以言说的情绪与内在感知。她关注个体在沉浸式环境中的身体反应与心理状态，试图在数字空间中建立一种更敏感、更具共情力的互动方式。

她相信，技术不仅是工具，也可以成为感知的延伸。通过游走于现实与虚构之间的数字空间，她的作品引导观众进入一种更安静、更内省的观看状态，在影像、空间与身体的微妙互动中，重新感受自己。

description_en:
The mixed reality installation Human-Computer (人机) addresses a critical cultural and ethical question: how do we safeguard human intentionality within automated computational workflows? While modern AI frameworks lean toward autonomous production, this work repositions the machine as a collaborative partner subordinate to human gesture, intuition, and spirit.

Grounded in the artist’s "Body Calligraphy" research, the project translates the traditional, two-dimensional act of writing into an immersive, three-dimensional spatial performance. Using real-time motion tracking and spatial computing, the system logs the precise acceleration, deceleration, and kinetic pathways of the artist’s body. This physical data is then piped into a custom digital environment where it acts as the primary driver for volumetric ink rendering.

By mapping somatic inputs directly into the computational space, Human-Computer ensures that every virtual stroke hanging suspended in the MR environment remains anchored to a genuine human origin. The technology does not replace the artist; instead, it provides a digital topology that visualizes the invisible currents of momentum, space, and time. Through this fluid feedback loop between human movement and responsive code, the work serves as both a digital experiment and a manifesto, demonstrating a harmonious AGI-era workflow where cultural heritage and human consciousness maintain absolute agency.
description_cn:
混合现实交互装置《人机》直面了一个关键的文化与伦理命题：在自动化计算工作流日益普及的今天，我们该如何捍卫人类的创作主体性？当现代人工智能趋向于自主生成时，本作品将机器重新定位为一个服务于人类手势、直觉与精神的协同媒介。

作品依托艺术家的“体书”研究，将传统的二维书写行为转化为沉浸式的三维空间身体表演。通过实时动作捕捉与空间计算技术，系统精确记录下艺术家身体运动的加速度、减速度与空间轨迹。这些物理数据随后被导入定制的数字环境中，成为驱动三维容积水墨渲染的核心底层数据。

通过将躯体输入直接映射到计算空间，《人机》确保了悬浮于MR环境中的每一道虚拟笔触都牢牢锚定于真实的人类源头。技术在此处并非取代艺术家，而是提供了一种数字拓扑结构，将气韵、空间与时间等无形动能具象化。通过人类运动与响应式代码之间的流体反馈闭环，该作品既是一次数字艺术实验，也是一份艺术宣言，展示了一种在AGI时代下、由传统文化遗产与人类意识占据绝对主导权的和谐人机协作范式。
artist_bio_en:
Pierre Yishao Shum is an interdisciplinary artist, architect, and researcher working at the intersection of traditional Chinese culture, spatial design, and immersive media. He earned his Master of Arts in Architecture from the Royal College of Art, London, which grounded his understanding of spatial structures, and subsequently completed his PhD at the School of Creative Media, City University of Hong Kong, where he focused on computational art and interactive systems.

Yishao’s artistic practice investigates how historical artistic disciplines can be deconstructed and reborn within digital topographies. Specifically, his work focuses on translating the dimensional restraints of traditional two-dimensional calligraphy into immersive, multi-sensory spatial performances. By leveraging real-time engines and mixed reality (MR), he treats human gesture as a generative data source, expanding the somatic experience of writing into physical environments.

Based between Hong Kong and Beijing, Yishao actively contributes to the discourse on Digital Humanities and spatial computing. His work seeks to move beyond mere digital preservation, aiming instead to establish a new vernacular for heritage—one where computing technology and subtle data systems act as mediums to reflect, respond to, and amplify the kinetic energy of human tradition.
artist_bio_cn:
岑逸少是一位跨学科艺术家、建筑师及学者，长期致力于将中国传统文化、空间设计与沉浸式媒体进行深度融合。他于英国皇家艺术学院建筑系获得硕士学位，奠定了其深厚的空间结构与美学思维；随后于香港城市大学创意媒体学院取得博士学位，专注研究计算艺术与交互系统的创新应用。

岑逸少的艺术实践核心在于探讨历史艺术范式在数字拓扑空间中的解构与重塑。他尤为关注如何将传统二维水墨书写的局限性，转化为全方位、多感官的沉浸式空间表演。通过利用实时渲染引擎与混合现实（MR）技术，他将人类的身体律动视为一种生成式数据源，将书写的躯体经验扩展至现实物理空间之中。

现活跃于香港与北京两地的他，积极参与数字人文与空间计算领域的学术与艺术思辨。他的创作旨在超越单纯的数字复刻，转而为文化遗产建立一种全新的“当代语汇”——在这一语汇中，计算技术与底层数据系统作为媒介，去映射、回应并放大人类传统律动中的无形动能

description_en:
When you step before the mirror, you do not see yourself clearly. Your reflection is there — but over it, constituting it, is a point cloud: the tracking system's rendering of your body as discrete spatial data. You appear first as the mirror has already processed you, not as light returning from glass but as coordinates in a computational space. The technical apparatus does not hide itself. It surfaces first. 

Then a sphere appears, floating. It is positioned so that your point cloud can occlude it — reach toward it and the visual overlap is real. Something responds. This is the first discovery: your data-body has weight in this space.  As you move, the world emerges. A fantastical natural environment grows out of the geometric skeleton — plant-animal hybrid forms, translucent structures that are flower and fish simultaneously, metallic-organic branches that look like both skeleton and living tissue. The world does not pre-exist your presence. It is generated by it. 

And as the world appears, your technical self recedes. The point cloud dissolves. By the time the environment is fully present, what you see in the mirror is only your optical reflection — continuous, analog, the body as light — moving through a world it called into being. The data-body has been absorbed. What began as apparatus has become milieu.  Before you leave, a flower — generated by your interaction with the mirror — waits by the exit. It is the one thing the mirror lets you take --- a tertiary retention made portable: the technical memory of your encounter. 

《共生》 stands at another location on campus. It is not a replica of the mirror experience. It is what the mirror's world looks like when it has detached from the glass and the body both — the same individuating forms, encountered without the interaction that made them. You may find it before or after the mirror. Either way, it has already been waiting.
description_cn:
站在镜前，你看到的并非清晰的自己。你的倒影在那里，但在它之上，与它共同构成它的，是一团点云：追踪系统对你身体的渲染，将你呈现为离散的空间数据。你最初以镜子已经处理过你的方式出现——不是光从玻璃上返回，而是计算空间中的一组坐标。技术装置并不隐藏自己，它率先浮现。 

随后，一个球体出现，悬浮在前。它的位置经过设计，使你的点云恰好能够遮挡它——向它伸手，视觉上的重叠是真实的。有什么东西回应了。这是第一个发现：你的数据之身，在这个空间里有重量。 
随着你的移动，世界开始浮现。一个奇幻的自然环境从几何骨架中生长而出——植物-动物混合形态，半透明的结构同时是花也是鱼，金属-有机的枝干既像骨骼也像活体组织。这个世界并非预先存在，它由你的在场所生成。 

而随着世界的显现，你的技术性自我也逐渐隐退。点云消散。当环境完全呈现时，你在镜中看到的只剩下你的光学倒影——连续的、模拟的、身体作为光的存在——在一个由它自身召唤而出的世界中移动。数据之身已被吸收。最初作为装置存在的东西，已成为环境。离开之前，一朵由你与镜子的互动所生成的花，在出口处等待着你。那是镜子允许你带走的唯一之物 --- 那是一份可携带的第三持留：你此次相遇的技术记忆。

《共生》驻立在校园的另一处空间。它不是镜中体验的复制。它是镜子的世界脱离了玻璃与身体之后的形态——同样的个体化形式，在没有生成它们的那场互动的情况下被遭遇。你可能在遇见镜子之前先遇见它，也可能在之后。无论如何，它一直在那里等待。
artist_bio_en:
Qiushi Zhou is an Assistant Professor at Computational Media and Arts Thrust and Internet of Things Thrust of Information Hub at HKUST (GZ). With broad interest in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Qiushi’s research focuses on building and understanding fundamental interaction techniques for future XR interfaces. The main themes of his work include novel eye+hand input techniques in XR, creative use of augmented mirrors in both practical and artistic contexts, and theoretical and historical reflections on interaction design concepts and paradigms. Qiushi serves as Program Committee and Editorial Board members for top HCI venues, including CHI, UIST, and ISS. He has collaborated with global industry leaders in XR, including Google, Meta, and Logitech, and with renowned artists to build interactive installations exhibited at galleries and festivals in Australia.

Yilin and Xuanyi are students of Dr. Qiushi Zhou. Their research interests lie in exploring new interaction methods.
artist_bio_cn:
罗伊琳是学习交互艺术的学生。她的研究兴趣集中在人机交互（HCI）领域，尤其关注与镜子相关的扩展现实交互。她探索如何将反射表面重新构想为交互界面，并研究其在扩展现实环境中重塑感知、身体感与空间交互的潜力。

张轩逸是香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术（CMA）学域的博士研究生。经由横跨艺术策展与数字媒体的学术背景，其研究立足于人机交互、技术哲学及批判性媒体研究的交汇点。他的研究旨在对弥散于当代生活的各类技术物展开批判性探究，并将这些技术系统视为蕴含丰富文化、社会及哲学意涵的关键场域。通过整合上述跨学科领域，他致力于探索人类与其所栖居的技术环境之间那些微妙而复杂的关系。

杨剑玮目前是暨南大学硕士研究生，研究兴趣包括人机交互、扩展现实与虚拟现实交互技术。他主要关注沉浸式环境中的交互方式设计、用户行为分析与用户体验评估。

周秋实是香港科技大学（广州）信息枢纽计算媒体与艺术学域以及物联网学域的助理教授。他对人机交互（HCI）有广泛的兴趣，研究重点是给未来的扩展现实（XR）界面构建基础性的交互技术。
他的主要研究主题包括：XR中结合眼动与手部输入的新型交互技术、增强镜在实用与艺术语境中的创新应用，以及对交互设计概念与范式的理论与历史反思。
他曾担任多个人机交互顶级会议（包括CHI、UIST和ISS）的程序委员会成员及期刊编委。他还与全球XR行业领军企业（包括Google、Meta和Logitech）开展合作，并与知名艺术家合作打造互动装置作品，这些作品曾在澳大利亚的画廊与艺术节中展出。

title_en: Mycelial Memories: A Living Archive of Deep Time
title_cn: 菌丝记忆：地质深时的活体档案
description_en: Mycelial Memories is an immersive virtual reality installation that reimagines mycelial networks as living archives bridging temporal boundaries through immersive VR experiences. Drawing on anthropomorphism as a methodological framework, this work translates non-human fungal perception into human perceivable language, creating an experiential meditation on memory, time, and ecological interconnection. Participants navigate a bioluminescent digital forest where diverse mushroom species preserve and present fragments of human civilization across AI-mediated past, present and future. By positioning mycelial networks as alternative models of documentation and memory, the installation challenges anthropocentric narratives and proposes a multispecies perspective to understanding human history within broader ecological timescales.
description_cn: 《菌丝记忆：深时的生命档案》是一件沉浸式虚拟现实装置，将菌丝网络重新想象为跨越时间边界的生命档案。作品以拟人化作为方法框架，把非人类的真菌感知转译为人类可感知的语言，形成一次关于记忆、时间与生态互联的体验式冥想。参与者穿行于一片生物发光的数字森林，在那里，不同种类的蘑菇保存并呈现由 AI 中介的过去、现在与未来中的人类文明碎片。通过将菌丝网络视为另一种记录与记忆模型，装置挑战以人类为中心的叙事，并提出一种多物种视角，以更广阔的生态时间尺度理解人类历史。
artist_bio_en:
Artist, Technical Curator.
Azure Zhang is having her PhD study in HKUST-GZ. She completed her master studies at the Royal College of Art and University College London. With expanding knowledge in computer science, HCI, and material craft, she demonstrates a strong interest in interdisciplinary research. Her current research interest is examining the anthropomorphism embedded in both scientific research and art practice, challenging claims to non-human perspectives, with a thematic focus on geological contexts. She has exhibited in various international locations, including Museu Nacional Da República Brazil, Munich Jewellery Week, London Wellcome Collection, and Shanghai M50 Art Zone, K11 and The Bund, etc. Azure Zhang is a Leonardo LASER talk featured speaker, her master thesis was invited to present at FIT New York during a symposium. Additionally, in 2021, she held two solo exhibitions on her physical artwork UNFOLD YOUR BODY 1.0 and 2.0 in Shanghai. description_en: Ocean of Whales is an immersive Mixed Reality (MR) interactive installation that operates at the critical intersection of technological intervention, post-natural ecology, and speculative biology. By positioning the majestic, primordial form of the whale as a living canvas for "AI mutations," the artwork offers a profound critique of the Anthropocene, proposing a future where human-induced ecological shifts permanently rewrite the morphological blueprints of marine life. The project departs from traditional ecological documentation; instead, it utilizes computational systems to simulate a techno-evolutionary trajectory. Here, the whale is no longer merely a biological entity but an algorithmic ecosystem, adapting to an environment saturated with digital artifice and environmental trauma. Through embodied interaction, Ocean of Whales transforms the passive spectator into an active participant within this speculative evolutionary narrative. The MR interface establishes a cognitive and emotional bridge between the human participant and the mutating leviathans, challenging viewers to confront the consequences of corporate and technological overreach. The artistic concern lies in the blurriness of the boundary between the organic and the synthetic. By witnessing the radical transfiguration of one of Earth’s most ancient species through the lens of artificial intelligence, the audience is forced to contemplate a chilling yet mesmerizing reality: a future where the survival of nature depends entirely on its capacity to become artificial. Ultimately, Ocean of Whales serves as both an elegiac tribute to the disappearing pristine wilderness and a radical advocacy for a new collective consciousness regarding our planet's fragile morphological future.
description_cn: 《鲸海》（Ocean of Whales）是一件沉浸式混合现实（MR）互动装置作品，立足于技术干预、后自然生态学与思辨生物学的核心交汇点。作品将远古而雄浑的鲸鱼形态作为“AI变种”的生命画布，对“人类世”带来的生态巨变进行了深刻的省思。本作品彻底告别了传统的生态纪录式叙事，转而利用计算系统来模拟一条“技术-进化”的潜在轨迹。在这里，鲸鱼不再仅仅是一个纯粹的生物个体，而是一个算法驱动的生态系统，它正在被迫适应一个充斥着数字人造物与环境创伤的未来世界。通过具身化的空间互动，我们将原本被动的旁观者转化为这场思辨进化叙事中的参与者。MR界面在人类观众与变异巨兽之间搭建起一座认知与情感的桥梁，迫使观众直面人类技术扩张给自然带来的深远后果。创作者的艺术关切核心在于有机物与合成物之间日渐模糊的界限。当观众亲眼目睹地球上最古老的物种之一在人工智能的干预下发生如此剧烈的形态流变，一种冰冷却又迷人的现实感油然而生：在未来的某个奇点，自然的幸存或许不得不依赖于其自身的“人造化”。最终，这个作品不仅是对行将消逝的纯粹荒野的一曲挽歌，更是一份激进的宣言，旨在唤醒公众对于地球脆弱物种形态未来的集体反思与生态守护意识。

description_en: Las Awichas (Grandmothers) unfolds through eight interconnected stories, where time and boundaries between humans and animals dissolve. Each Awicha has a spirit animal—jaguar, hummingbird, condor, gecko, spider, whale, monkey, llama—reimagined as robots from the future carrying the past in their mechanical parts. Their narratives play out in the exhibition space as a metaphor for how our grandmothers made us part of this world and it's now our turn to shape its future. Born as children of time, we find ourselves between past and future—destroying natural resources, yet somehow we manage to survive. To truly live, we must embrace life's cycle: dying so that others may be born. A quirky, childlike narrator guides us through a rich soundscape of orchestra, jungle, city, and mechanical textures. Las Awichas is a Pandora's box of spatial storytelling and the cyclical nature of time.
description_cn: 《拉斯·阿维查斯》（祖母们）以八个相互关联的故事展开，时间和人类与动物之间的边界在其中消解。每位阿维查（祖母）都有自己的灵兽——美洲虎、蜂鸟、秃鹰、壁虎、蜘蛛、鲸鱼、猴子和骆马——这些动物在展览空间中被想象为来自未来、体内携带着过去记忆的机器人。她们的故事作为隐喻在展览空间上演，正如我们的祖母让我们成为这个世界的一部分，如今轮到我们去塑造世界的未来。作为时间的孩子，我们身处过去与未来之间——既毁坏着自然资源，却又奇迹般地存活下来。真正的生命在于拥抱生命的轮回：逝去才能带来新生。一个古灵精怪、孩童般的叙述者带领我们穿越交响乐、丛林、城市与机械质感交融的丰富音景。《拉斯·阿维查斯》是一只潘多拉的盒子，讲述了空间叙事与时间循环的奥秘。
artist_bio_en:
